facts.text: Oatman was named after Olive Oatman, a girl captured by Native Americans in 1851 whose survival story became a regional symbol.
The town sprang to life in 1915 when prospectors struck gold worth $10 million, turning it into a bustling boomtown for a decade.
The oldest two‑story adobe in Mohave County, still standing, earned historic landmark status and is a reminder of Oatman’s early days.
A 1921 fire destroyed many buildings but spared the 1902 Oatman Hotel, which later claimed a rumored honeymoon suite for Clark Gable and Carole Lombard.
Oatman’s Wild West vibe endures with staged shootouts on Main Street and burros roaming the streets, a quirky tradition that began when miners brought the animals.
The town sits on the longest remaining stretch of historic Route 66, a fact that once drew travelers between Kingman and Needles before the highway was rerouted.
